title: Solo developer rebuilds Adobe Creative Suite in Rust using Claude, releases it free to all
key_facts: Reddit user u/ai_art_is_art posted on r/creativecloud about a suite of alternatives to Adobe products, built with Claude; the post was later removed but a comment with GitHub links remains.
Tools named include PhotoCraft, LightCraft, ImageCraft and FilmCraft; all are built in Rust and free to download.
The developer plans to reach 100% parity with Adobe's features within a month.
The software is agent-native: AI can use its tools and menus through a JSON control channel and an MCP server.
Some commenters warn of a lawsuit; replies say it is a clean-room reimplementation and no Adobe code was used.
Skeptics warn about unverified AI-written code; a Sonar 2026 survey of 1,100 developers found 96% do not fully trust AI-generated code.
Commenters also warn about safety and actual functionality.
quote_evidence: Their post has since been removed, but their comment with links to their GitHub page remains.
responses to those warnings state that it is a clean-room reimplementation and no Adobe source code was used or copied in the creation of the software.
why_it_matters_hint: A free Adobe-style suite is promised, but the code is unchecked and the legal position is disputed.
event_date: Reddit post date not stated; Tom's Hardware published 8 Oct 2026
notes: Single outlet reporting on an anonymous Reddit post; claims of parity are the developer's.
